sketch.title: Funnel then chain
sketch.caption: This is a funnel-into-chain: the piece narrows from a broad problem (how do neurons process information?) down to one precise tool (partial information decomposition), then follows that tool out through evidence, practical limits, and future extensions.

scenes.title: Overview

items.text: How do brains process information?
Old limits: too little data, too few tools
Mutual info & transfer entropy track flow
But flow alone misses how inputs combine
PID: redundant, unique, synergistic information
Synergy concentrated in rich clubs
Recurrent connections boost synergy
In behaving monkeys, synergy shifts to redundancy during movement
Caveats: bivariate estimates, cultures not live brains
Practical limits: data, tools, scalability
Future: time-resolved & multi-target PID
Neurons compute on patterns, not just totals

scenes.caption: The article funnels from a broad open question down to one analytic tool, then chains that tool through evidence, practice, and future work.

scenes.title: Building the PID framework

items.text: Joint information need not equal sum of parts
Whole > parts = synergy; whole < parts = redundancy
Two parents: split into redundant, unique, synergistic atoms
Equations underdetermined without more assumptions
General case: a lattice of information-sharing atoms
Mobius inversion computes each atom's unique value
No single agreed redundancy measure — must choose one

scenes.caption: A chain that builds intuition from a simple two-neuron case up to a general lattice, which still needs a choice of redundancy measure to actually compute.

scenes.title: PID in action: the empirical findings

items.text: Record hundreds of cortical neurons, run PID on triads
Synergy tracks feedforward information flow strength
Rich-club neurons account for ~88% of network synergy
More recurrent connections, more synergy
Synergy peaks at moderate input correlation, then falls as it turns redundant
Together: computation concentrates in dense, correlated hubs
Caveats: bivariate TE bias, cultures not live circuits
In behaving macaques, rich-club synergy pattern replicates
Redundancy rises during motor execution, for signal reliability

scenes.caption: Several independent empirical findings from cultured and living brains converge on the same picture: synergy, genuine information processing, clusters where connections are dense and inputs are moderately correlated, and shifts with behavior.

plates.title: The Funnel and the Chain
plates.prompt: A tall illuminated manuscript page, sepia ink and faint gold leaf on aged, lightly stained parchment, read top to bottom like a scroll of connected roundels joined by a single winding vine-line that stands for the flow of information through the whole page. No lettering appears anywhere except the small capitalized titles beneath each scene. At the very top: SIGNALS FROM THE SURROUNDINGS, a cutaway brain receiving rays from a drawn landscape, a small figure acting below. The vine descends to ARRAY OF ELECTRODES, fine probes lowered into a dense field of dot-neurons. It continues to SOURCE AND TARGET, two small linked circles joined by one thread, then to STREAMS THAT INTERACT, two threads braiding and crossing above them. The vine then enters a modestly framed panel — a thin rectangular border drawn but unlettered — containing THE OVERLAPPING CIRCLES: a red circle and a blue circle overlapping inside a larger oval, the overlap tinted purple. From this framed panel the vine forks in two and both branches enter a second, larger enclosure gathering four scenes: THE DENSE RICH CLUB, a glowing tight knot of interlinked figures, beside THE LOOPING TRIAD, two source-figures connected by a looping line into a third target figure; both branches then converge downward into REACH AND GRASP, a monkey's arm reaching and gripping with its signal-line drawn doubled over; from there a single line leads to THE OVERESTIMATED EDGE, one connecting line shadowed by a faint crack, still within the large enclosure's lower edge. The vine exits the enclosure and descends to COMBINATIONS OF ONES AND ZEROS, a ledger-grid overflowing with 0 and 1 marks, then to THE INFORMATIONAL TIME SERIES, a ribbon strung with red, blue, and purple beads of changing size. At the foot of the page, PATTERNS, NOT TOTALS: a target-neuron figure facing an arrangement of differently shaped signal-marks, tilting toward the pattern. Palette: warm sepia line work throughout, with the red/blue/purple used only for the information-circle and bead imagery, as the article itself colours them. Generous parchment margins, scenes large and clear, no crowding, no marginal ornament beyond the single connecting vine.

plates.title: Building the Lattice
plates.prompt: A tall illuminated manuscript page in sepia ink on aged parchment, the same hand and palette as the overview page, read top to bottom as a single descending chain. No lettering anywhere except the eight small capitalized titles beneath each scene. At the top, framed in a thin unlettered border exactly as it appeared on the overview page, THE OVERLAPPING CIRCLES: a red circle and a blue circle overlapping within a larger oval, the overlap tinted purple, drawn as an archway opening onto the chain below. Through the archway, the vine-line descends to MANY PARENTS, ONE DECISION: many small parent-neuron figures sending converging lines into one larger neuron who gathers them with drawn hands. Below it, INTEGRATING COMPUTATION: the same gathering figure now actively knotting the threads into one braided cord. The line continues to TWO PARENTS, ONE TARGET: exactly two parent figures each sending a single line onto one target figure, a simpler, cleaner version of the scene above. Next, THREE KNOWN, FOUR UNKNOWN: a balance scale with three weights resting on one pan and four bare hooks dangling empty from the other. The vine-line then widens into THE FINITE SET OF ATOMS: a branching trellis of small distinct knots rising in tiers, assembled directly below the scale. From the trellis, WHAT LIES BELOW: a hand reaching upward through the tiers, touching each knot in turn, finding something at each level not present below it. At the foot of the page, A DOZEN COMPETING RULERS: a row of roughly a dozen different measuring rods and calipers laid side by side, with a scholarly hand selecting one. Palette: warm sepia linework throughout, with red, blue, and purple reserved only for the opening circles, matching the overview page. Keep the scenes large, evenly spaced down the page, bare parchment around them, no crowding and no marginal ornament beyond the single connecting vine-line.

plates.title: The Evidence Converges
plates.prompt: A tall illuminated manuscript page in sepia ink on aged parchment, same hand and palette as the other plates, read top to bottom. No lettering anywhere except the nine small capitalized titles beneath each scene. At the top, ARRAYS OVER CULTURED NEURONS: a flat dish studded with a grid of fine electrode points over scattered cultured neuron-figures. The vine-line forks into three parallel branches set side by side across the width of the page: on the left A QUARTER OF THE FLOW, a three-figure triad with a quarter-filled glowing measure beside its feedforward line; in the middle THE DENSE RICH CLUB, a tightly knotted, brightly glowing cluster of figures; on the right THE LOOPING TRIAD, two source-figures joined by a looping line feeding a third target figure. Below these three, a fourth branch enters from the side: PEAK AT SEVEN PERCENT, two source-figures whose shared glow swells toward a small marked point on a dial before fading. All four branches are drawn gathered downward by a single hand into one bundled cord in GATHERING THE THREADS, descending toward a loose cluster of cortical rich-club figures. From this gathering point a single line continues down to THE OVERESTIMATED EDGE, one connecting line marked with a faint crack. The line then leads to THREE MACAQUES AT WORK, three seated macaque figures with fine signal-lines rising from their heads toward recording equipment. Finally, at the foot of the page, REACH AND GRASP: one macaque reaching out and closing its hand around an object, its signal-line to the hand drawn doubled and tripled over. Palette: warm sepia linework throughout, with the red/blue/purple circle-colouring reserved only for the glow effects in A QUARTER OF THE FLOW, THE DENSE RICH CLUB, THE LOOPING TRIAD and PEAK AT SEVEN PERCENT, matching the earlier plates. Keep every scene large and legible, using the full width of the page for the three-way fork, bare parchment around the scenes, no crowding, no marginal ornament beyond the connecting vine-lines.

questions.question: If mutual information and transfer entropy already track dependence and directed flow between neurons, why is a further decomposition framework even needed?

passages.quote: Information transfer captures the overall “flow” of information through the system; however, it is limited in its ability to reveal how different streams of information “interact” and how neurons produce novel or modified information from multiple sources

questions.question: How do you tell whether a neuron's joint input is doing extra computation versus just repeating what each source already said on its own?

passages.quote: If the left-hand side of Equation (4) (the “whole”) is greater than the right-hand side (the sum of the “parts”), then there is some information about Y that is disclosed by the joint state of all the neurons that is not disclosed by any individual parent.

questions.question: If there's no single accepted way to define redundant information, how solid is the whole decomposition into redundant, unique, and synergistic parts?

passages.quote: Unfortunately, classical Shannon information theory provides no unique solution to any of these, and so considerable work has been devoted to developing formal measures of each.
To date, no single universally accepted measure has been proposed.

questions.question: Why does synergy stop rising and start falling once the source neurons' activity becomes similar enough, instead of just increasing indefinitely?

passages.quote: Past this level, the synergy began to decrease (this level is marked by the vertical dotted line in Figure 4E).
This suggests that as the similarity of the converging information grows past some point, it becomes redundant, and the total amount of synergistic output is suppressed.

questions.question: The culture studies built their effective networks using bivariate transfer entropy, but doesn't that risk overstating which connections even belong in the analyzed triads?

passages.quote: This matters because it has been shown that bivariate analyses overestimate the significance of bivariate edges [51].

questions.question: Given how artificial cultured brain slices are, do the synergy patterns found there actually hold up in a real, behaving animal?

passages.quote: the demands placed on a circuit in the context of a behaving animal are certain to differ from those placed on cultures in vitro.
Despite this difference, many aspects of the in vitro results were successfully replicated in animal models, including the presence of a rich club and an increase in synergy in high-degree nodes.

questions.question: Does finding synergy in a neuron actually explain why it computes that way, or just describe a statistical pattern without a mechanism?

passages.quote: it does not necessarily provide a mechanistic explanation for why particular neurons are synergy-dominated or redundancy-dominated.

questions.question: Since the number of PID pieces explodes combinatorially with more inputs, how can this approach ever handle real neurons that receive input from many sources?

passages.quote: This sequence of numbers grows appallingly fast: in the case of six parent neurons, there are 7,828,354 distinct PI atoms, the vast majority of which are difficult to interpret.

questions.question: Given that entropy and mutual information estimates from finite data are known to be biased upward, could the reported synergy be a statistical artifact rather than real computation?

passages.quote: it is known that the plug-in estimator for the Shannon entropy consistently underestimates the true entropy and overestimates the mutual information

questions.question: What two things historically limited the study of neural information processing, according to the article?
questions.referenceAnswer: A lack of enough data to infer complex patterns of dependence among many neurons, and a lack of adequate analytical tools to extract insight from that data.

evidence.quote: The first was a lack of appropriate data, since the analysis of synergistic dynamics requires large amounts of data to accurately infer the structure of multivariate dependence.
The second was a lack of appropriate analytical approaches.

questions.question: What technological development eased this data limitation?
questions.premise: One of the two limitations was a lack of enough data.
questions.referenceAnswer: New electrical and optical recording technologies that can record from hundreds or thousands of neurons at sub-millisecond resolution.

evidence.quote: with innovative new electrical and optical recording technologies that can record from hundreds or thousands of neurons at sub-millisecond temporal resolution, this limitation has abated considerably

questions.question: What does mutual information measure about the activity of two neurons?
questions.referenceAnswer: It measures how much knowing one neuron's state reduces uncertainty about the other's, an undirected measure of instantaneous dependence that says nothing about time-directed flow between them.

evidence.quote: It does not, however, quantify information transfer between the neurons, as it is an undirected measure that describes the instantaneous dependency between two variables

questions.question: What does transfer entropy add that mutual information lacks?
questions.premise: Mutual information is undirected and carries no notion of time-directed flow.
questions.referenceAnswer: Transfer entropy quantifies how much a source neuron's past activity reduces uncertainty about a target neuron's future activity, beyond what the target's own past already explains, capturing directed information flow.

evidence.quote: TE(X → Y) is read as the transfer entropy from X’s past to Y’s future.

TE is understood as quantifying how much the past of the source variable reduces our uncertainty about the future of the target variable, after accounting for information disclosed by the target variable’s own past (autocorrelation).

questions.question: Why is information transfer, even directed transfer entropy, still not enough to reveal how neurons process information?
questions.premise: Transfer entropy measures directed information flow between a source and a target.
questions.referenceAnswer: Because it only captures the overall flow of information between pairs of neurons and cannot reveal how different incoming streams of information interact or combine to produce new or modified information.

evidence.quote: Information transfer captures the overall “flow” of information through the system; however, it is limited in its ability to reveal how different streams of information “interact” and how neurons produce novel or modified information from multiple sources

questions.question: In the partial information framework, what does it mean when the joint information two source neurons carry about a target together is greater than the sum of what each carries alone?
questions.referenceAnswer: It means the sources carry synergistic information about the target, disclosed only by their joint states and not by either source individually, reflecting an integrating computation.

evidence.quote: then there is some information about Y that is disclosed by the joint state of all the neurons that is not disclosed by any individual parent. In this case, the system exhibits synergistic dynamics

questions.question: What does it mean instead when the whole is less than the sum of the parts?
questions.premise: When the whole exceeds the sum of the parts, that excess is synergy.
questions.referenceAnswer: It means there is redundant information about the target that is carried by more than one source neuron and gets double-counted when their individual contributions are added up.

evidence.quote: Conversely, if the whole is less than the sum of its parts, then there must be redundant information about Y instantiated multiple times over the parent neurons that is “double counted” when summing the marginals.

questions.question: In the two-parent case, what four components does partial information decomposition split the total joint information into?
questions.referenceAnswer: Redundant information shared by both sources, the unique information each source alone provides, and the synergistic information only available from their joint states.

evidence.quote: where Red(X₁, X₂;Y) is the information about Y that could be learned by observing X₁ or X₂, Unq(Xᵢ;Y) is the information about Y that could only be learned by observing Xᵢ, and Syn(X₁, X₂;Y) is the information about Y that can only be learned by observing the joint states of X₁ and X₂ together.

questions.question: Why can't classical Shannon information theory alone pin down the values of these four components?
questions.premise: The decomposition has four unknown components: redundancy, two unique terms, and synergy.
questions.referenceAnswer: Because the resulting system of equations is underdetermined, with only three known mutual-information values but four unknown partial-information terms, so an additional measure of redundancy must be defined to solve it.

evidence.quote: The result is an underdetermined system of linear equations, with three known values (the mutual information terms) and four unknown values (the partial information terms).

questions.question: What complication arises when extending this decomposition from two parent neurons to three or more?
questions.premise: Solving the decomposition requires defining a redundancy measure.
questions.referenceAnswer: The number of distinct partial-information components grows much faster than the number of known mutual-information equations, so the simple two-source approach no longer works and a more elaborate lattice-based structure is needed.

evidence.quote: in the case of three or more parents, the resulting system of equations is not as constrained as in the two-element case, as the number of distinct partial information atoms grows much faster than the number of known mutual information terms.

questions.question: Why is there no single universally accepted way to measure redundant information?
questions.referenceAnswer: Because every proposed redundancy measure has trade-offs, such as only working for a fixed number of sources, only applying to discrete variables, or requiring arbitrary thresholds, so different contexts call for different choices.

evidence.quote: All measures have their own trade-offs and drawbacks (such as only being defined for systems of a fixed size, only being amenable to discrete random variables, or requiring arbitrary thresholds).

questions.question: In the cortical culture recordings, how did synergy relate to the amount of feedforward information propagation (transfer entropy) across groups of three neurons?
questions.referenceAnswer: Synergy was strongly positively correlated with a triad's transfer entropy, and was reliably about a quarter of that transfer entropy value.

evidence.quote: the amount of synergy observed in a given triad was reliably about a quarter of the transfer entropy for that triad

questions.question: How much more synergy did triads located inside network rich clubs show compared to triads outside them?
questions.premise: Synergy correlated strongly with how much information propagated through a triad.
questions.referenceAnswer: Rich club triads had about 2.7 times as much synergy as non-rich-club triads, and accounted for roughly 88% of all network-wide synergy despite rich club neurons being less than 40% of all neurons.

evidence.quote: the triads inside the rich clubs had 2.7 times the amount of synergy as the triads not in the rich club
the rich club triads accounted for ∼88% of the network-wide synergy

questions.question: How did the number of recurrent connections between source neurons, versus feedback connections from the target back to the sources, relate to synergy in a triad?
questions.referenceAnswer: More recurrent connections between source neurons were linked to greater synergy, while feedback connections tended to slightly reduce synergy rather than increase it.

evidence.quote: triads with more recurrent connections also had greater synergy [4]. Feedback connections were less predictive of synergy but tended to correlate with reduced synergy.

questions.question: At short, synaptic-range timescales, how did synergy relate to the similarity between the two source neurons' spiking activity?
questions.referenceAnswer: The greater the mutual information (similarity) between the source neurons at synaptic timescales, the greater the synergy, meaning more processing occurred where similar information streams converged.

evidence.quote: The greater the mutual information between source neurons at the synaptic timescale, the greater the synergy [3]. More information processing occurs where similar information streams converge

questions.question: What happened to synergy as timescales were extended well beyond the synaptic range and source similarity kept increasing?
questions.premise: At short timescales, synergy rose as the source neurons' activity became more similar.
questions.referenceAnswer: Synergy only increased up to a point, peaking when the source neurons' mutual information reached about 7% of its maximal possible value, and then decreased as redundancy took over at higher similarity.

evidence.quote: Interestingly, synergy only increased up to a point. The peak in synergy occurred when the mutual information was about 7% of the maximal value, regardless of the timescale. Past this level, the synergy began to decrease

questions.question: In the behaving-primate study, how did the balance between synergy and redundancy change during movement execution, such as a reach-and-grasp action?
questions.referenceAnswer: Although brain activity was generally synergy-dominated, the relative amount of redundant information increased dramatically during movement execution, likely to ensure reliable transmission of the 'move' signal to distant muscles.

evidence.quote: while brain activity was generally synergy-dominated (as opposed to redundancy-dominated), during movement execution (a reach-and-grasp action) the relative abundance of redundant information increased dramatically.

questions.question: Why does the growth in the number of partial-information components limit how practical PID is for neurons with many inputs?
questions.referenceAnswer: The number of distinct partial-information atoms grows extremely fast with the number of parent neurons, so for neurons with many inputs a complete decomposition becomes computationally intractable.

evidence.quote: This sequence of numbers grows appallingly fast: in the case of six parent neurons, there are 7,828,354 distinct PI atoms

questions.question: What does local PID make it possible to construct from neural recordings?
questions.referenceAnswer: A time-resolved 'informational time series' showing the redundant, unique, and synergistic information sharing at each individual moment, rather than only an overall expected value.

evidence.quote: The local PID framework allows us to perform the same decomposition, but for every individual possible configuration of specific source and target states. questions.question: What does the existence of synergy in neural recordings suggest about how neurons combine their inputs, according to the article's summary?
questions.referenceAnswer: It shows neurons do not simply sum their inputs and fire based on the total, as a basic threshold model would predict, but are instead sensitive to the particular patterns of incoming activity, with this synergistic processing shaped by each neuron's local network environment and the organism's behavioral state.

evidence.quote: The existence of synergy in empirical data shows us that neurons do not appear to blindly sum the number of inputs and fire in response to the total (as would be expected from a basic threshold model or complex contagion model), but instead they are also sensitive to the particular patterns of incoming stimuli.

ideas.name: Effective (statistically inferred) connectivity is treated as if it were real circuit structure
ideas.statement: Edges and motifs (feedforward, feedback, recurrent, rich club) inferred from thresholded transfer-entropy networks built on bivariate spike-train statistics are discussed as if they were actual synaptic connections, even though they are statistical inferences that can misrepresent true circuit wiring.
ideas.whyYouNeedIt: Without treating effective-network edges as stand-ins for real synapses, claims like 'triads inside the rich club process more information' or 'recurrent connections increase synergy' would be statements about correlational networks rather than about neural circuits, and the whole structure–function narrative would not go through.

occurrences.quote: Analyzing the effective connectivity among neurons using transfer entropy enables extraction of the full effective network upon which the spiking dynamics occurred. The computational triads, consisting of two neurons (source neurons) connecting to a common third neuron (target neuron), can then be identified.
occurrences.reasoning: Moves directly from a statistically inferred effective network to talk of 'computational triads' as if they were concrete circuit elements, without which the later topology claims would not be about circuits at all.

occurrences.quote: the functional networks from which triads were drawn and against which the synergy values were compared were generated from bivariate transfer entropy analyses. This matters because it has been shown that bivariate analyses overestimate the significance of bivariate edges
occurrences.reasoning: This later caveat only makes sense as a correction to an assumption, used throughout the empirical sections, that the inferred edges reliably reflect real connectivity.

ideas.name: Mutual information tracks correlation; transfer entropy tracks directed flow
ideas.statement: Mutual information is an undirected measure of statistical dependence between two signals (akin to functional connectivity), while transfer entropy measures how much a source's past specifically reduces uncertainty about a target's future beyond the target's own history (akin to effective, directed connectivity).

occurrences.quote: It does not, however, quantify information transfer between the neurons, as it is an undirected measure that describes the instantaneous dependency between two variables and has no notion of the time-directed structure that we intuitively understand as "transfer" or "flow."
occurrences.reasoning: Explicitly denies that mutual information captures directed flow, setting up the need for a separate, directional measure.

occurrences.quote: Whereas mutual information is a measure of functional connectivity, transfer entropy measures effective connectivity [14]. In other words, transfer entropy provides a measure of information propagation.
occurrences.reasoning: States the contrast directly as functional versus effective connectivity.

ideas.name: Synergy as the signature of genuine computation
ideas.statement: When the information that two or more neurons jointly carry about a target's future state is greater than the sum of what each carries on its own, that extra, unshareable chunk (synergy) marks a genuine integration or 'computation' performed on the combined pattern, not reducible to any single input.

occurrences.quote: then there is some information about Y that is disclosed by the joint state of all the neurons that is not disclosed by any individual parent. In this case, the system exhibits synergistic dynamics, and the target neuron can be thought of as performing a kind of integrating "computation" on all of its inputs considered jointly
occurrences.reasoning: States directly that the mathematical surplus (whole minus sum of parts) is to be read as the neuron performing computation.

occurrences.quote: Information transfer captures the overall "flow" of information through the system; however, it is limited in its ability to reveal how different streams of information "interact" and how neurons produce novel or modified information from multiple sources
occurrences.reasoning: Frames the whole motivation for PID around capturing this synergistic, pattern-sensitive production of information as distinct from mere flow.

ideas.name: PID decomposes joint information into redundant, unique, and synergistic atoms via a lattice
ideas.statement: Partial information decomposition splits the total information that a set of sources carries about a target into non-overlapping pieces (shared/redundant, unique to each source, and synergistic across combinations), computed by arranging all source subsets into a partially ordered lattice and using Mobius inversion once a redundancy function is chosen.

occurrences.quote: given a suitable measure of redundancy (which we will refer to as I∩(·)), it is possible to decompose the total joint mutual information into a finite set of unique, partial information atoms based on how all the elements of S share information about Y.
occurrences.reasoning: States the core decomposition machinery that the rest of the PID formalism depends on.

occurrences.quote: Given this partially ordered lattice structure and our redundancy function I∩(·), it is possible to recursively quantify the value of every partial information atom (Π(α)) via Mobius inversion:
occurrences.reasoning: Gives the specific mathematical mechanism (lattice plus Mobius inversion) that converts a redundancy function into the full decomposition.

occurrences.quote: it was not until the seminal work of Williams and Beer [1] that it was recognized how to algebraically decompose the total joint mutual information into the particular contributions of the parts (and higher-order ensembles of parts)
occurrences.reasoning: Credits the origin of the lattice-based decomposition idea that underlies every later application described in the piece.

ideas.name: No single agreed redundancy measure exists, and the choice matters
ideas.statement: Because classical information theory does not pin down a unique definition of 'redundant information,' researchers must choose among roughly a dozen competing redundancy functions, each with different assumptions, trade-offs, and domains of applicability, and that choice changes the resulting decomposition.

occurrences.quote: Unfortunately, classical Shannon information theory provides no unique solution to any of these, and so considerable work has been devoted to developing formal measures of each.
occurrences.reasoning: States plainly that the underdetermined system has no canonical solution, motivating the need to pick a redundancy function.

occurrences.quote: To date, no single universally accepted measure has been proposed. All measures have their own trade-offs and drawbacks (such as only being defined for systems of a fixed size, only being amenable to discrete random variables, or requiring arbitrary thresholds).
occurrences.reasoning: Makes explicit that the lack of a standard measure is a live practical problem, not a solved technicality.

ideas.name: Recurrent connections boost synergy; feedback connections do not
ideas.statement: Among the three connection types in a source-source-target triad, more connections between the two source neurons (recurrent) reliably increase synergistic integration, while connections from the target back to the sources (feedback) do not reliably increase it and may even slightly reduce it.

occurrences.quote: Using PID, we found that triads with more recurrent connections also had greater synergy [4]. Feedback connections were less predictive of synergy but tended to correlate with reduced synergy.
occurrences.reasoning: States the asymmetric effect of recurrent versus feedback connectivity on synergy directly.

occurrences.quote: Recurrent connections are connections between the source neurons. Again, there may be zero, one, or two recurrent connections. The question for our analysis was whether synergistic integration was sensitive to the number of feedback or recurrent connections.
occurrences.reasoning: Defines the connectivity motifs whose differential effect on synergy is the point of the idea.

ideas.name: Synergy peaks at intermediate source correlation, not maximal correlation
ideas.statement: As the similarity (mutual information) between two converging input streams increases, synergy first rises but then falls past a certain point, while redundancy keeps rising, so the relationship between input correlation and higher-order computation is non-monotonic rather than ever-increasing.

occurrences.quote: The greater the mutual information between source neurons at the synaptic timescale, the greater the synergy [3]. More information processing occurs where similar information streams converge
occurrences.reasoning: States the initial positive relationship that sets up the surprise of the later reversal.

occurrences.quote: Interestingly, synergy only increased up to a point. The peak in synergy occurred when the mutual information was about 7% of the maximal value, regardless of the timescale. Past this level, the synergy began to decrease
occurrences.reasoning: States the non-monotonic peak-and-decline pattern that distinguishes this idea from a simple positive correlation.

ideas.name: The balance of synergy and redundancy shifts with task demands and brain region
ideas.statement: The relative dominance of synergistic versus redundant information in a circuit is not fixed but changes depending on the behavioral epoch and brain region, for example shifting toward redundancy during motor execution where reliable signal duplication may be favored over integrative computation.

occurrences.quote: The researchers found that while brain activity was generally synergy-dominated (as opposed to redundancy-dominated), during movement execution (a reach-and-grasp action) the relative abundance of redundant information increased dramatically.
occurrences.reasoning: States the task-dependent shift from synergy-dominance to redundancy-dominance directly.

occurrences.quote: These results show not only that synergistic information dynamics is a feature of ongoing, spontaneous neural activity but also that synergy seems to reflect behaviorally specific patterns of dynamical activity in the cortex.
occurrences.reasoning: Draws the general conclusion that synergy's expression is behaviorally specific rather than a fixed circuit property.

ideas.name: Local and multi-target extensions generalize PID beyond static, single-target snapshots
ideas.statement: Classic PID computes redundancy, uniqueness, and synergy as expected values averaged over an entire probability distribution and for one target at a time; newer variants localize the decomposition to single moments in time (local PID) or extend it to multiple targets and temporal structure (integrated information decomposition), opening up time-resolved and richer multivariate analyses.

occurrences.quote: The local PID framework allows us to perform the same decomposition, but for every individual possible configuration of specific source and target states. In the context of neural recordings, the obvious application of this is the construction of a time-resolved, "informational time series"
occurrences.reasoning: States the move from averaged to moment-by-moment decomposition, which is the core of the local PID idea.

quotes.text: There are many basic unanswered questions about information processing. What types of circuit connectivity are most favorable for neural information processing? How is neural information processing affected by the overall structure and correlations present in incoming information flows? What are the physiological correlates of information processing at the level of neural circuits? Are distinct transformations promoted by distinct physiological systems? Do distinct transformations relate to the demands of different environmental or behavioral tasks?
quotes.reason: Lays out the open questions the whole review is organized around

quotes.text: Historically, there have been two key limitations hindering the study of information processing by neural circuits. The first was a lack of appropriate data, since the analysis of synergistic dynamics requires large amounts of data to accurately infer the structure of multivariate dependence. Until recently, such data were difficult to access. In the last decade, however, with innovative new electrical and optical recording technologies that can record from hundreds or thousands of neurons at sub-millisecond temporal resolution, this limitation has abated considerably. The second was a lack of appropriate analytical approaches.
quotes.reason: States the two historical bottlenecks that motivate the entire review

quotes.text: Mutual information [12] can measure the dependence in the spiking between two neurons
quotes.reason: introduces the core tool used to quantify dependence between neurons

quotes.text: I(X;Y) measures how our ability to correctly infer the state of X changes, depending on whether we are accounting for (potentially) shared dependencies with Y. It can be thought of as a nonlinear correlation between two patterns of activity [3,13].
quotes.reason: gives the intuitive meaning of mutual information in plain terms

quotes.text: It does not, however, quantify information transfer between the neurons, as it is an undirected measure that describes the instantaneous dependency between two variables and has no notion of the time-directed structure that we intuitively understand as “transfer” or “flow.”
quotes.reason: clarifies a key limitation of mutual information that motivates transfer entropy

quotes.text: Whereas mutual information is a measure of functional connectivity, transfer entropy measures effective connectivity [14]. In other words, transfer entropy provides a measure of information propagation.
quotes.reason: crisp distinction between the two core measures used throughout the paper

quotes.text: Information transfer captures the overall “flow” of information through the system; however, it is limited in its ability to reveal how different streams of information “interact” and how neurons produce novel or modified information from multiple sources [19].
quotes.reason: states the gap that motivates moving from transfer entropy to partial information decomposition

quotes.text: If the left-hand side of Equation (4) (the “whole”) is greater than the right-hand side (the sum of the “parts”), then there is some information about Y that is disclosed by the joint state of all the neurons that is not disclosed by any individual parent. In this case, the system exhibits synergistic dynamics, and the target neuron can be thought of as performing a kind of integrating “computation” on all of its inputs considered jointly (this is also sometimes referred to as “information modification” in the literature [19]). Conversely, if the whole is less than the sum of its parts, then there must be redundant information about Y instantiated multiple times over the parent neurons that is “double counted” when summing the marginals.
quotes.reason: defines synergy and redundancy, the two central concepts of the whole framework

quotes.text: This inequality has been recognized for decades; however, it was not until the seminal work of Williams and Beer [1] that it was recognized how to algebraically decompose the total joint mutual information into the particular contributions of the parts (and higher-order ensembles of parts).
quotes.reason: credits the foundational insight that the whole review builds on

quotes.text: where Red(X₁, X₂;Y) is the information about Y that could be learned by observing X₁ or X₂, Unq(Xᵢ;Y) is the information about Y that could only be learned by observing Xᵢ, and Syn(X₁, X₂;Y) is the information about Y that can only be learned by observing the joint states of X₁ and X₂ together.
quotes.reason: plain-language definitions of redundant, unique, and synergistic information

quotes.text: The result is an underdetermined system of linear equations, with three known values (the mutual information terms) and four unknown values (the partial information terms). If any of the unknown terms can be defined, then the other three emerge “for free”. Unfortunately, classical Shannon information theory provides no unique solution to any of these, and so considerable work has been devoted to developing formal measures of each.
quotes.reason: explains the core mathematical problem that makes choosing a redundancy function necessary

quotes.text: In the absence of a single accepted measure, different contexts may require the choice of different functions.
quotes.reason: key practical caveat about the lack of a universal redundancy measure

quotes.text: The majority of the studies discussed in this paper used the original Imin measure proposed in [1], although this measure has been criticized for unintuitive behavior [29,39].
quotes.reason: flags a methodological limitation underlying most of the empirical results discussed

quotes.text: By definition, rich clubs are disproportionately dense in information propagation: 20% of the neurons account for 70% of the information propagation in organotypic cortical cultures [49].
quotes.reason: concrete, striking statistic establishing why rich clubs matter for information flow

quotes.text: Unambiguously, rich club triads processed more information than triads outside rich clubs. Numerically, the triads inside the rich clubs had 2.7 times the amount of synergy as the triads not in the rich club (Figure 4B). Due to rich clubs having a high density of triads and rich club triads having a greater synergy per triad, a majority of the network-wide synergy was accounted for by rich club triads. Despite the fact that that less than 40% of the neurons were in the rich club, the rich club triads accounted for ∼88% of the network-wide synergy.
quotes.reason: central empirical finding linking network structure to information processing, with striking numbers

quotes.text: Using PID, we found that triads with more recurrent connections also had greater synergy [4]. Feedback connections were less predictive of synergy but tended to correlate with reduced synergy. Numerically, in comparison to the simplest computational triads (those with no feedback or recurrent connections), triads with two recurrent connections and no feedback connections had 50% more synergy (Figure 4C). Triads with two feedback connections but no recurrent connections had 10% less synergy than the simplest computational triads.
quotes.reason: key empirical result distinguishing feedforward, feedback, and recurrent contributions to synergy

quotes.text: The result was unambiguous. The greater the mutual information between source neurons at the synaptic timescale, the greater the synergy [3]. More information processing occurs where similar information streams converge (Figure 4E, the three leftmost panels for synaptic timescales).
quotes.reason: states a clean, surprising empirical relationship between input similarity and synergistic computation

quotes.text: Interestingly, synergy only increased up to a point. The peak in synergy occurred when the mutual information was about 7% of the maximal value, regardless of the timescale. Past this level, the synergy began to decrease (this level is marked by the vertical dotted line in Figure 4E).
quotes.reason: nontrivial nonmonotonic finding showing synergy is maximized at intermediate input correlation

quotes.text: This suggests that as the similarity of the converging information grows past some point, it becomes redundant, and the total amount of synergistic output is suppressed.
quotes.reason: interprets why synergy peaks rather than growing indefinitely with correlated input

quotes.text: The researchers found that while brain activity was generally synergy-dominated (as opposed to redundancy-dominated), during movement execution (a reach-and-grasp action) the relative abundance of redundant information increased dramatically.
quotes.reason: shows that information processing style shifts with behavioral demands, extending the lab findings to real behavior

quotes.text: This increase in relative redundancy was interpreted as a response to the practical requirements of the task: during motor execution, the brain needs to send the “move” signal to distant muscles, and to ensure high-fidelity transmission the brain may duplicate information many times over (minimizing the risk of a single corrupted signal leading to erroneous behavior).
quotes.reason: offers a vivid functional explanation for why redundancy rises during motor execution

quotes.text: These results show not only that synergistic information dynamics is a feature of ongoing, spontaneous neural activity but also that synergy seems to reflect behaviorally specific patterns of dynamical activity in the cortex.
quotes.reason: summarizes the significance of the primate findings for the paper's broader thesis

quotes.text: One important caveat to note with respect to PID applied to neural data is that while it provides a powerful framework for recognizing statistical dependencies between neurons, it does not necessarily provide a mechanistic explanation for why particular neurons are synergy-dominated or redundancy-dominated.
quotes.reason: honest limitation distinguishing statistical description from mechanistic explanation

quotes.text: The most significant is the explosive growth of the PI lattice. For a system with k parent neurons, the number of distinct PI atoms is given by the kth Dedekind number (minus two) [30]. This sequence of numbers grows appallingly fast: in the case of six parent neurons, there are 7,828,354 distinct PI atoms, the vast majority of which are difficult to interpret.
quotes.reason: vivid, concrete illustration of the scalability problem facing PID

quotes.text: Given that single neurons can receive inputs from very large numbers of upstream neurons, a “complete” description of the information dynamics of any individual neuron is completely intractable.
quotes.reason: stark statement of a fundamental practical limit of the framework

quotes.text: The existence of synergy in empirical data shows us that neurons do not appear to blindly sum the number of inputs and fire in response to the total (as would be expected from a basic threshold model or complex contagion model), but instead they are also sensitive to the particular patterns of incoming stimuli.
quotes.reason: the paper's closing thesis stated plainly, tying the whole review together

entries.name: Partial Information Decomposition
entries.senseHere: A mathematical method that splits the total information two or more sources carry about an outcome into separate pieces: information both sources share, information only one source has, and information that only appears when you look at the sources together.
entries.background: Introduced by Williams and Beer as a way to formally resolve the long-standing puzzle that information from multiple sources does not simply add up.

entries.name: Rich club
entries.senseHere: The subset of best-connected neurons in a recorded circuit whose connections to each other are denser than would occur by chance; in the article these neurons account for a disproportionate share of both information flow and synergistic computation.

entries.name: Mutual information
entries.senseHere: A measure of how much knowing one variable's state reduces uncertainty about another, used here as a kind of nonlinear correlation between two neurons' activity patterns.

entries.name: Transfer entropy
entries.senseHere: A directional measure of how much knowing a source neuron's past activity reduces uncertainty about a target neuron's future activity, beyond what the target's own past already tells you.

entries.name: Functional connectivity
entries.senseHere: A description of how similar or correlated two neurons' activity patterns are, without implying one directly influences the other, as captured by mutual information.

entries.name: Effective connectivity
entries.senseHere: A description of directed influence from one neuron's activity onto another's future activity, as captured by transfer entropy, distinct from mere correlation.

entries.name: Synergy
entries.senseHere: The portion of information about a target neuron's activity that can only be learned by observing two or more source neurons jointly, not from any one alone. It is treated in the article as the signature of genuine neural 'computation' or integration.

entries.name: Redundant information
entries.senseHere: Information about a target that could be learned equally well by observing just one source or just another, so it gets double-counted if you naively add up each source's individual information.

entries.name: Unique information
entries.senseHere: Information about a target neuron that only one particular source discloses, not available from any other source in the set.

entries.name: Williams and Beer
entries.background: Researchers credited with originally proposing the partial information decomposition framework, providing the first systematic way to split joint information among multiple sources into separate components.

entries.name: Redundancy function
entries.senseHere: A formally chosen rule for measuring exactly how much information counts as redundant between sources; without picking one, the decomposition into redundant, unique, and synergistic pieces is mathematically unsolvable.

entries.name: Computational triad
entries.senseHere: A basic unit of analysis consisting of two source neurons that both connect to one shared target neuron, used as the simplest case for applying partial information decomposition.

entries.name: Partial information lattice
entries.senseHere: A structured diagram of every possible combination of sources that could share information about a target, ordered so each combination's unique contribution can be calculated by subtracting out simpler combinations beneath it.

entries.name: Mobius inversion
entries.senseHere: The mathematical procedure used to work through the partial information lattice step by step, calculating each combination's distinct contribution by removing what is already accounted for by simpler combinations below it.

entries.name: Organotypic culture
entries.senseHere: A slice of mouse cortical tissue grown in a dish that preserves much of the original circuit's natural connectivity, allowing researchers to record from hundreds of real neurons at once.

entries.name: O-information
entries.senseHere: A simplified, faster-to-compute measure that approximates whether a group of variables is overall more redundant or more synergistic, used as a practical stand-in when full decomposition is too complex.

entries.name: Dedekind number
entries.senseHere: A rapidly growing count used here to describe how many distinct information-sharing combinations exist once more than a couple of source neurons are considered, explaining why full decomposition quickly becomes computationally impossible.

entries.name: Local PID
entries.senseHere: A version of partial information decomposition calculated for each individual moment or specific pattern of activity, rather than averaged over all possibilities, enabling a time-by-time trace of redundancy, uniqueness, and synergy.

entries.name: Neuronal avalanche
entries.senseHere: A cascading burst of neural activity treated in the article as a hallmark of complex, self-organized dynamics, whose internal structure can be analyzed with time-resolved information decomposition.
entries.background: A commonly studied pattern in cortical networks where activity propagates in bursts of varying sizes following statistical patterns associated with systems poised near a critical point.

entries.name: Integrated information decomposition
entries.senseHere: An extension of partial information decomposition that handles multiple target variables at once, for instance decomposing how the past of several variables jointly shapes the future of several others.

entries.text: Neural information processing remains poorly understood; this review stakes a method for actually finding it in data.
Data and tools once blocked this search; both now exist, but the analytic method itself is not yet laid out.
Flow between neurons can now be tracked; whether tracking flow reveals genuine processing is still unanswered.
Flow alone cannot show how inputs combine into output; a way to decompose that combination is proposed but not yet built.
A formal decomposition into redundant, unique, and synergistic information now exists; which measure of redundancy to use remains unsettled.
Applied to real circuits, synergy turns out concentrated in hubs, recurrent loops, and correlated inputs, and shifts with task; but shown only in cultures and limited primate data.
The framework delivers real findings, yet matching measures, tools, and sample size to the data limits how far it can be pushed.
Newer variants promise finer, time-resolved, multi-target views of processing; these remain early extensions, not yet widely tested.
Settled: neurons compute on patterns, shaped by network position and task; open: what biological machinery actually produces that computation.
